additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states that the ten types of melody ARE a bechina of simcha: 'כִּי יֵשׁ עֲשָׂרָה מִינֵי נְגִינָה, שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת שִׂמְחָה'. This is then confirmed in reverse: 'שִׂמְחָה, שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת יוּד מִינֵי נְגִינָה'. This is a symmetric bechina equation — simcha IS the ten melodies and the ten melodies ARE simcha. The ten types of melody belong in Package 1 as an expression of the same essential reality as simcha, tikkun hacholeh, and the circle dance.
additions.source_quote: כִּי יֵשׁ עֲשָׂרָה מִינֵי נְגִינָה, שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת שִׂמְחָה... שִׂמְחָה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת יוּד מִינֵי נְגִינָה

analysis_notes.notes: All 4 nodes from the 2 bechina edges are assigned to the single package — no orphans. The third edge with reference 1024 is type 'eitza' (שמחה → רפואה) and correctly belongs between packages rather than within them (simcha PRODUCES healing, rather than being identified with it). One missing bechina concept was identified from the source text: 'יוד מיני נגינה' (the ten types of melody), which the Rebbe explicitly equates with simcha in both directions using bechina language. The 'יוד מיני דפיקין' (ten pulse types) also appears prominently in the text, but its relationship to the ten melodies is causal (the melodies animate the pulses), not bechina — so it is correctly not added to Package 1. The evil/negative domain — 'מרה שחרה' and 'עצבות' (melancholy and sadness) — appears as the opposition to simcha throughout the teaching, but the Rebbe does not identify them with bechina language (no 'X הוא בחינת Y' formulation), presenting them instead as the cause of illness. They are therefore not proposed as additions to any package. This Torah is unusually compact, with the entire bechina structure conveying a single unified message: simcha, its embodied form as dance, and healing are all one essential reality.
